output.summary: KEP-5978 proposed a cluster-scoped ClusterResourceClaimTemplate in Kubernetes so Pods and PodGroups could reference a shared template by name. The KEP was withdrawn and the capability is to be built out-of-tree instead.
output.rationale:
Reviewers questioned whether cluster admins would actually manage ClusterResourceClaimTemplates, since ResourceClaims are normally part of the workload itself. Maintainers judged that a ClusterResourceClaimTemplate only adds value as an admin-level abstraction, and that the in-tree API surface was not justified for 1.37. The group agreed to move the idea to an out-of-tree controller that copies templates into namespaces.</rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">Withdrawn because the maintainers concluded that the feature is most appropriately done out-of-tree, and they did not want to add the in-tree API surface for 1.37. The sources say "we don't proceed with this KEP for 1.37 (and potentially never)" and that the decision was to "withdraw this KEP".</outcome_reason>
<parameter name="alternatives">[{"option":"Pod field resolves to a namespaced ResourceClaimTemplate and falls back to a ClusterResourceClaimTemplate of the same name","why_not":"liggitt said ambiguous resolution is hard to reason about and can cause race conditions, and it changes the meaning of the field for existing clients."}, {"option":"Separate ResourceClaimTemplateRef field with kind (ResourceClaimTemplate or ClusterResourceClaimTemplate)","why_not":"pohly said having two equivalent ways to reference a template is confusing; he preferred a separate clusterResourceClaimTemplateName field."}, {"option":"Authorize ClusterResourceClaimTemplate usage by checking whether the pod's service account can get the template","why_not":"pohly said the controller has no credentials of the user who created the reference, and that referencing a cluster template grants no extra privileges."}, {"option":"Separate CRD and controller that generates namespaced ResourceClaimTemplates","why_not":"Not chosen as the in-tree path; it was instead the basis of the out-of-tree direction the group settled on (a controller copying RCTs from a special namespace)."}]

evidence.quote: I think that's reasonable. @troychiu WDYT? Instead of doing this in-tree, we create a separate controller in k-sigs? We would therefore withdraw this KEP.
I think that makes sense. Maintaining an out-of-tree controller looks good enough. I have marked this KEP as `withdrawn`.
ClusterResourceClaimTemplate makes sense when it will be used as an additional abstraction between cluster admin and users
We decided that it is most appropriately done out-of-tree. For example, a controller that copies RCTs from a special namespace to other namespaces (that's one approach).
ambiguous reference resolution from an object depending on what else exists at a given point in time is pretty hard to reason about
